key_insight: A scalable Bayesian Gaussian process classifier improved uncertainty calibration and predictive performance in breast cancer histopathology benchmarks, with the largest gains under hospital-level distribution shift.
clinical_relevance: Better-calibrated predictions could support more reliable cross-hospital pathology AI, but benchmark results do not establish clinical safety or benefit.
method: Extract frozen histopathology embeddings with the Phikon foundation model.
Use accelerated RPCholesky for low-rank kernel approximation and selected pivots for prediction.
Sample the Bayesian posterior using non-centered Hamiltonian Monte Carlo at approximately 300,000 training points.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on PCam and CAMELYON17-WILDS reported up to 88% lower expected calibration error and up to 90% lower false negative rate versus stochastic variational GP and neural network baselines.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish prospective clinical performance or computational requirements for routine deployment.
paper_title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
